clue.text: Wealthy Scot come to bad end in 'Yorkshire town

parts.note: wealthy means rich
mon is the Scots form of man, so a Scot is a MON

indicators.note: the end of the word bad is its last letter, signalled by 'come to bad end'

explanation.surface: A rich Scotsman meets a sorry fate somewhere in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come to' joins the pieces; 'end' takes only the last letter of 'bad'. Richmond is a market town in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Richmond is a historic market town in North Yorkshire, England.

clue.text: A criminal set ?

explanation.definitionFit: A receiver is someone who handles stolen goods, a fence; a radio or TV set picks up broadcast signals.

clue.text: Artist appearing in ""Z cars " ?

explanation.definitionFit: John Constable was an English landscape painter; Z Cars was a British TV police drama whose leads were police officers of that lowest rank.

clue.text: Hammers in Rugby encounters

explanation.definitionFit: To maul someone is to batter them; in rugby a maul is a scrum-like tussle round the player holding the ball.

clue.text: Incompetent big-wig?

explanation.definitionFit: Split as two words it says 'unable', lacking skill; a notable is an important, distinguished person.

clue.text: Like to include grain for pig-food ?

indicators.note: one word is made to include another, so the grain goes inside the word for like

parts.note: as means like (as in 'as a child')
corn is a grain

explanation.surface: Something similar, with cereal added, to feed the pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Oak nuts were traditionally used to fatten pigs, turned out into woods to forage.

clue.text: Frank took courses — he wanted the job

parts.note: frank means candid, open
to take the courses of a meal is to eat them, so took courses means ate

explanation.surface: An honest applicant who sat through a meal was keen on the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took courses' looks like study but means eating the courses of a dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: An applicant for a post is one who sought it.

clue.text: Montague Moore supplies materials

indicators.note: the name Moore supplies the raw materials, its letters, for something new to be built

explanation.surface: A man named Moore provides cloth and supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo is the Montague who loves Juliet in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's tragedy the young hero belongs to the house of Montague.

clue.text: Walks pompously in braces ?

explanation.definitionFit: To strut is to walk with a swagger; struts are bracing bars in a frame.

clue.text: Eccentrics have many rows

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword way of saying many
ranks are rows, as of soldiers

explanation.surface: Odd people own lots of quarrels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' suggests arguments but means lines; 'have' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Cranks are oddballs with fixed, peculiar ideas.

clue.text: A shocking guide ?

parts.note: a material that guides electric current along it, so it carries shocks, also an orchestra's or bus's guide

explanation.definitionFit: A wire or metal that lets current flow guides electricity, and a person leading an orchestra guides the players.

clue.text: It. is found in Belgium, or back in Rumania

indicators.note: back says the run of letters is read in the opposite direction
in says the letters sit inside the word Rumania

explanation.surface: A geography note: a place in Belgium, or else something in Romania.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the first five letters of RUMANIA, RUMAN, and 'back' turns them round. Namur is a city in southern Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Namur is a city and province of Wallonia in Belgium.

clue.text: This is cut in pieces, causing stress

indicators.note: something cut in pieces is broken up, so the letters of 'is cut' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something chopped up leads to tension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' stands for the answer: this is IS CUT broken 'in pieces'. ICTUS is the stressed beat in a line of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody the ictus is the rhythmic accent or beat falling on a syllable.

clue.text: Creature is a bow-legged bird we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words are judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: bow-legged is bandy and a coot is a water bird

explanation.surface: An animal described as a waterbird with bowed legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The bandicoot is a small Australasian marsupial, an animal.

clue.text: Include letter written to transport expert

parts.note: em is the name of the letter M
BR was British Rail, the UK national rail transport system
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A note sent to a transport specialist adds them to the list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written to' joins the pieces. BR stood for British Rail, which ran Britain's trains until the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace an idea or group is to take it in or comprise it.

clue.text: Room apt to contain painters, perhaps

indicators.note: one word is made to contain another, so the painters go inside apt

parts.note: painters are, for example, art men, men of art

explanation.surface: A fitting space to house some decorators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apt' looks like an adjective describing the room, but it is the container; 'perhaps' marks painters as one example of men of art.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a room or a suite of rooms in a building.

clue.text: Becky's notes

explanation.definitionFit: Becky Sharp is the heroine of Thackeray's Vanity Fair, so something is hers; raised semitones are written as sharp signs in music.

clue.text: Lack of 'comfort in VIP train nothing 'unusual

indicators.note: unusual says the letters before it are arranged in an out-of-the-ordinary way

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A VIP train with nothing out of the ordinary leaves passengers uncomfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges VIP, TRAIN and O; 'in' joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Privation is hardship, being without basic necessities.

clue.text: White protector might become chicken-hearted ?

parts.note: the case guarding an egg's white holds a chick at its heart if the egg is fertile, so it becomes chicken-hearted

explanation.definitionFit: The thin calcium casing of a hen's egg protects the albumen and in time encloses a growing chick.

clue.text: Before French was an illusionist

explanation.definitionFit: The French preposition for 'in front of' is devant; David Devant was a famous English stage magician.

clue.text: No 'go-ahead artist, apparently

explanation.definitionFit: One who turns round is not going ahead; J. M. W. Turner was the great English painter of light and sea.

clue.text: Supporter goes round Ireland looking sly

indicators.note: one piece goes round another, so the word for Ireland is placed inside the supporter

parts.note: a leg supports a table or body
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone who backs a team tours Ireland with a sly look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' could be a fan, but here it is a limb; the insertion lands after the limb's second letter, not in its exact centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A leering face wears a sly, knowing or lascivious look.

clue.text: Inside information from base ?

explanation.definitionFit: The low-down is the true inside story; low-down also means mean or contemptible.

clue.text: Philosopher — and. sound batsman

indicators.note: sound says the next word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: Jack Hobbs was a great English opening batsman

explanation.surface: A thinker, and a reliable cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like praise for the batsman but signals the homophone. Jack Hobbs was a famous Surrey and England cricketer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hobbes was the English thinker who wrote Leviathan.

clue.text: Defeat by means' of no ball?

explanation.definitionFit: To overthrow a ruler is to topple or vanquish them; in cricket an overthrow scores runs from a fielder's wild return rather than from a delivery bowled.

clue.text: Escape from girl of foreign type

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name
de is the French word for of

explanation.surface: Getting away from a woman of an alien kind.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade something is to dodge or elude it.

clue.text: Creditor is in short a stupid fellow; very stupid !

parts.note: CR is the standard short form of creditor in accounts
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A lender, put briefly, is a fool: in fact a complete idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in short' tells you creditor is abbreviated to CR.
explanation.definitionFit: Crass means grossly dense or insensitive, lacking all intelligence.

clue.text: College poet.

explanation.definitionFit: Clare is a Cambridge college; John Clare was an English rural poet.

clue.text: Means to stop in the thicket

explanation.definitionFit: A brake halts a vehicle; a brake is also an area of dense undergrowth or bracken.

clue.text: Tending to call up memories of the East case

parts.note: the vocative is the grammatical case used when addressing someone

explanation.surface: Something that brings back memories of the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the' joins the pieces. The vocative is the case of address in Latin grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: Evocative things summon up images, feelings or recollections from the past.

clue.text: Accommodation for a gladiator wishing to put up

definitions.text: Accommodation for a gladiator wishing to put up

parts.words: Accommodation for a gladiator wishing to put up
parts.note: a lodging for the sword a Roman fighter wants to put away, read as though he needs a room for the night

explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard holds a blade, housing a fighter's sword when it is put up, that is put away.
